newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas 19-share index won't include CANTV until September.
newsitem.headline: Caracas 19-share index won't include CANTV until September.

text.p: Peeved investors hoping Venezuela's arguably most closely-watched stock, telephone company CANTV, might finally be included in the Caracas bolsa's 19-share index, will have to wait until September, exchange officials said.
"We're waiting until the share has been trading for a while, until the price stabilizes," a bolsa spokesman told Reuters.
Investors complain that without CANTV, which made its debut last November in a $1 billion global offering, the Caracas bolsa's index fails to fully capture general stock exchange movements.
"You'd have thought they might throw caution to the winds and include the company," said Credit Lyonnais broker Peter Ryan.
"CANTV might be surging, but the IBC falling."

Instead, investors are turning to leading brokers' Merinvest and Bancaracas indices. Both are also market capitalization based that rise or fall with the value of a portfolio, such as Standard and Poor's 500 in the United States.
While market cap indices better reflect changes in a typical portofolio's value, they can also be easily skewed by large movements in the price of a single stock.
The other alternative is an index that moves with average changes in prices of a list of shares, such as the U.S.'s Dow Jones industrial average.
